conviction_note: Three dated, uncovered items (a quiet $5m retention plan vesting 31 Dec 2026, a Nasdaq compliance date five business days after the print whose stated cure is time-infeasible, and an interest-coverage covenant that is far tighter than the leverage covenant management cites) sum to about -8, partly offset by +2.5 for a -20.65% five-day de-rate I could find no informational cause for in a name with double-digit short interest; net -5.5, deliberately about a third of the 15.83% historical median because the distress itself is thoroughly priced at $0.5951.

findings.finding: A quiet 8-K filed 2026-04-17 (never press-released, absent from the company's own IR news feed) discloses a '2026 Retention Plan' with a $5,000,000 pool — roughly 9% of the ~$54m equity market cap — to keep executives 'during the pendency of the Company's strategic review process', vesting on the earlier of December 31, 2026 or 'certain milestone events or transactions'; that vest date is nine days after the December 22, 2026 debt maturity, which dates the board's own expected resolution to year-end rather than to this print, and makes the FY2027 guidance the CFO conditioned on 'completion of our strategic review' unlikely to appear on 2026-09-14.
findings.why_not_priced: This 8-K carries no item 2.02 and no press release, so it never reached a wire: StockTitan's HAIN feed jumps from 2026-03-02 (snacks sale completion) to 2026-05-04 with nothing in between, and the company's IR news page shows no April release. With one analyst estimate on the name there is no sell-side note to surface it. If the market had read it, the $5m accrual would appear in previews as a cost item against a $54m cap and the 'milestone events or transactions' vest trigger would be quoted as evidence the board expects a sale or restructuring rather than a plain refinancing; neither appears anywhere I could find.
findings.independence: Separate source, the Q3 FY26 call of 2026-05-11, has the CFO saying 'While it's too early to provide guidance on fiscal 2027... Upon completion of our strategic review, we plan to provide guidance for fiscal 2027' — https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/hain-celestial-hain-q3-2026-172930024.html (call date fixed independently by the 8-K item 2.02 filed 2026-05-11). Third, independent corroboration that the review was still open with no transaction: EDGAR shows zero 8-Ks of any item between 2026-05-11 and today — https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000910406&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40

findings.finding: The Nasdaq minimum-bid 180-day compliance date is 2026-09-21 — five business days after this print — and the cure the company itself named in the 8-K ('propose a reverse stock split to shareholders at its 2026 annual meeting') cannot complete in time, because Hain's annual meeting is held in early November (the 2025 meeting's item 5.07 8-K was filed 2025-11-05) and no PRE 14A or DEF 14A has been filed as of today; the only listing outcomes actually available in the week of the print are a transfer down to the Nasdaq Capital Market for a second 180 days, or a delisting determination.
findings.why_not_priced: The sweep is right that sub-$1 listing risk is generally known, but the specific arithmetic is not: the 8-K's own remedy is dated to a meeting that happens six weeks after the deadline, and the Capital Market transfer that is the only workable path is never mentioned in the filing. If this were priced, previews would be discussing a Capital Market downgrade or a special meeting rather than repeating the company's reverse-split sentence, and a preliminary proxy would exist on EDGAR by now — it does not.
findings.independence: Independent of the source above: the 2025 annual meeting date comes from the item 5.07 8-K of 2025-11-05 and the absence of any 2026 proxy from the EDGAR filing index — https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000910406&type=8-K&dateb=&owner=include&count=40

findings.finding: The binding financial covenant is the 2.00:1.00 minimum interest coverage ratio, not the 5.50:1.00 maximum net secured leverage ratio the CFO points to ('leverage of 4.3x... plenty of headroom under the covenant of 5.5x'): interest and other financing expense ROSE to $45.1m for the nine months to 2026-03-31 from $38.4m a year earlier despite a $101m term-loan paydown, because the September 2025 Fourth Amendment raised the Term SOFR margin from 3.00% to 4.00%, while the TTM adjusted EBITDA implied by the company's own disclosed ratios fell from about $138m at 2025-06-30 to about $118m at 2026-03-31 — putting coverage near 2.0-2.3x against a 2.00x floor at the June 2026 test date being reported on Monday.
findings.why_not_priced: Every public discussion of this credit agreement — the Q3 call, the coverage of it, the FY2025 release — quotes only the leverage test, which has 1.2 turns of headroom and looks comfortable; the coverage test added and reset by the Fourth Amendment is quoted nowhere. If the market had done this arithmetic, the interest-expense line rising year-on-year through a deleveraging would be the headline of every preview rather than the $155m of debt reduction. I flag the honest weakness: the covenant almost certainly tests Consolidated CASH Interest Expense, which excludes deferred-financing-fee amortisation that is large after two amendments, so true headroom could be a full turn wider — hence the wide band and the +1 upside bound.
findings.independence: The 5.50x leverage level and the 2.00x coverage level are confirmed from a DIFFERENT document, the company's FY2025 results release of 2025-09-15 and the Fourth Amendment description therein — https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/09/15/3149840/0/en/Hain-Celestial-Reports-Fiscal-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-Year-2025-Financial-Results.html — and the 100bp margin step-up from the amendment exhibit itself, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/910406/000119312525203534/hain-ex10_1-5.htm. NOTE: the EBITDA implication and the $45.1m interest figure both come from the same Q3 FY26 10-Q as the primary source, so treat that part as one document, not two.

findings.finding: The -20.65% five-day run-in has no informational cause I could locate: no 8-K of any item since 2026-05-11, no company press release since 2026-08-17, and HAIN is NOT among the ten S&P SmallCap 600 deletions announced 2026-09-04 effective 2026-09-21 — so the de-rate into the print is positioning and forced supply, not news, in a stock last reported 13.9% short.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the inverse case — it says part of what IS in the price is not information. The baseline shows 20-day run-up at only -0.82% against -20.65% over five days, i.e. the stock round-tripped a rally inside three weeks with no filing and no release to explain either leg. If the drop were news-driven there would be a document; I checked the S&P September rebalance, the full EDGAR index and the company's own newsroom and found none. At $0.5951 with no borrow-free option chain to hedge in, that sets up genuine squeeze risk on any constructive refinancing headline, and an 8-K item 1.01 signed in the last four business days would not yet be on file.
findings.independence: Two further sources, both distinct from the S&P release: the EDGAR filing index showing nothing but Schedule 13Gs since 2026-05-11 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000910406&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40) and the short-interest reading of 12,465,108 shares / 13.9% at the 2026-04-15 settlement (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/the-hain-celestial-group-inc-nasdaqhain-sees-large-increase-in-short-interest-2026-05-01/ — dated 2026-05-01 from the URL path, so five months stale and used only as context, not as the load-bearing fact).

searched_and_found_nothing: A covenant step-down at the June 2026 test date — I chased this hard because a search snippet gave a 4.75x/4.50x/4.25x schedule, and killed it: the September 2025 Fourth Amendment replaced that with a flat 5.50x from the quarter ending 2025-09-30 'and thereafter', confirmed in the company's own FY2025 release. Do not file it; it is stale text describing the superseded Third Amendment.
An S&P SmallCap 600 or index deletion as the cause of the five-day drop — HAIN appears nowhere in the 2026-09-04 rebalance announcement.
Any signed refinancing, maturity extension or lender amendment since 2026-05-11 — no 8-K item 1.01, no press release, nothing on the IR newsroom.

A baby-food heavy-metals litigation catalyst — the MDL (478 cases at 2026-08-03) has no scheduled bellwether trial, and the 2026-02-27 exclusion of most plaintiff causation experts ran in Hain's favour; nothing lands in this window.

An activist or distressed 13D — the July/August 13G cluster is routine quarterly filing, and the largest (Goldman Sachs Group, 5.8%, event date 2026-06-30) reports fractional share counts consistent with market-making inventory, not a position.
Nasdaq Hearings Panel or delisting-determination correspondence, a Form 25, an NT 10-K, or an auditor change (item 4.01) — none on file.
A usable option chain or any priced-direction anchor — the baseline's 942 contracts of total open interest and non-two-sided ATM legs mean there is no skew and no implied move to argue against.
App-store, subreddit and retail-forum chatter for a demand-side signal — nothing specific to the reporting quarter.
baseline_tension: There is no skew and no implied move to agree or disagree with, so the only baseline statement is the run-up, and my set cuts both ways against it: three findings push negative on a name already 72% off its high, while the fourth argues the -20.65% five-day leg was uninformed supply and should partly reverse — which is also what the repo's free control (-run_up_20d_pct, here only -0.82%) would say is close to flat.
